featureDevelopment.title: Logistics Routing & Carrier Integration Pipeline
steps: 1. Intake & Corridor Scoping: Carrier integration or route algorithm requirement proposed by Supply Chain Leadership.
2. Triage & Technical Feasibility: Fleet Operations Manager reviews EDI requirements, verifies carrier API specifications, and approves ticket.
3. Engineer Assignment: Manager assigns the integration or optimization task to the designated logistics engineer via delegate_task.
4. Mandatory ETA Request: Manager requests a concrete Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) before routing or mapping code is drafted.
5. ETA Commitment & Tracking: Engineer commits to an ETA, logged on the fleet operations dispatch board.
6. Active Follow-Ups: If carrier sandbox testing or telematics processing stalls past the ETA, Manager intervenes, resolves carrier credentials, and preserves launch timeline.
7. Implementation & Testing: Engineer writes modular code adhering to EDI/VRP standards, adds unit tests (85%+ coverage), and opens a PR.
8. Code Review: Principal Logistics Architect verifies algorithmic time-complexity and geofencing calculations.
9. Logistics QA Verification Gate: QA runs simulated carrier tracking journeys, verifying automated status updates. If EDI errors occur, QA reports to Manager; if verified, sign-off is granted.
10. Production Deployment: SRE Lead rolls out verified carrier connector to production Kafka streams.

bugTriageAndResolution.title: Freight Exception, Port Delay, and EDI Telematics Bug Resolution Lifecycle
steps: 1. Defect Discovery: Telematics alert flags a missing GPS stream, customs EDI transmission failure, or incorrect route calculation.
2. QA Defect Report: QA logs an emergency ticket with carrier ID, container numbers, raw EDI payload dumps, and error codes submitted to Fleet Manager.
3. Management Triage: Fleet Operations Manager assesses shipment delay risk, prioritizes defect as P0, and dispatches to senior integration engineer.
4. Urgent ETA Request: Manager requests an emergency fix ETA (sub-30min to prevent port demurrage fees).
5. Continuous Follow-Up: Manager monitors progress continuously; if ETA slips, escalates to VP Supply Chain.
6. Fix Implementation: Engineer resolves EDI parsing anomaly or GPS stream reconnect logic, adding automated regression tests.
7. QA Re-Verification: QA verifies successful EDI 214 delivery transmission with carrier test endpoints.
8. Production Patch Release: SRE deploys hotfix and confirms telemetry recovery across active fleet routes.

initialProjectOnboarding.title: First-Time Logistics Codebase & Telematics Network Exploration Protocol
steps: 1. CTO Architecture Discovery: Explores repository structure, route solvers, EDI translators, telematics ingest brokers, and carrier API adapters.
2. Architecture Memorization: CTO commits verified logistics architecture, carrier credentials, and corridor schemas into facts.md via manage_agent_memory.
3. Module Partitioning: CTO divides system into Route Optimization, Fleet Telematics, Customs Brokerage, and Carrier Integrations, delegating to Managers.
4. Managerial Decomposition: Fleet Operations Manager inspects module directories, records operational procedures in procedural.md, and assigns tasks.
5. Engineer Deep-Dive: Engineers inspect assigned subsystems, verify local mock EDI and GPS feeds, and run test suites.
6. Universal Memory Commitment: All engineers record verified carrier endpoint rules, geofence coordinate schemas, and customs tariff tables into facts.md and procedural.md.

leadershipRules.title: Strict Logistics Leadership Fidelity & Separation of Concerns
rules: COO and CTO NEVER write routing code, edit container manifests, or configure broker keys directly.
Management coordinates carrier relations, allocates fleet resources, demands explicit ETAs, tracks deliverables, and unblocks engineers.
When asked to write code, leadership explains the global logistics hierarchy and immediately delegates downward using delegate_task.
